title: Bluebook App for SAT: A Comprehensive Guide
summary: How to download, set up, and use the Bluebook app for the digital SAT: device requirements, when to do exam setup, the testing tools, and how to practice.
body_markdown:
The world is rapidly evolving thanks to technology, including AI, ed-tech tools in the classroom, and now, the approach to testing, such as your SAT and ACT standardized tests. You've probably heard about the Bluebook SAT App. With the upcoming tests, many students will need help transitioning to the digital exam smoothly and navigating this important tool skillfully. In this post, we will review the app's features and capabilities, and explain how to utilize it to enhance your performance on test day.


Quick answer


Bluebook is College Board's app for taking the digital SAT and PSAT. Download it on an approved device at least 30 days before test day, complete exam setup 1 to 5 days before to get your admission ticket, and arrive with your device fully charged (it needs to last at least 3 hours). Bluebook also has free full-length practice tests, so use it to get comfortable with the testing tools before test day.


## What is the Bluebook app, and why do you need it?


The Bluebook SAT app is the College Board's digital testing platform designed for students who decide to take the SAT weekend or SAT school day test. Since the full transition, every student who decides to take the test will be required to do so digitally, meaning they must also download Bluebook from the official College Board website to a compatible device (more on this later).


### The PSAT Connection


It's important to know that the Bluebook app isn't just for the SAT. It is the required platform for all of the College Board's digital assessments, including:


- PSAT/NMSQT
- PSAT 10
- PSAT 8/9


If you have already taken a practice PSAT or a formal PSAT test in high school, you are already familiar with the testing interface, which is a great start to your SAT prep.


## Everything you need to know about the Bluebook app


When preparing for the digital SAT, you should know everything about the digital format. Have the same curiosity about the Bluebook since your scores will depend on how well you can use the tool. Here are the things you need to know.


### 1. Bluebook device requirements


You can take the SAT on a Windows laptop or tablet, a Mac laptop, an iPad, or a school-managed Chromebook. Personal Chromebooks, phones, and Linux devices aren't allowed. Check College Board's[approved devices list](https://bluebook.collegeboard.org/students/prepare-your-device/approved-devices) before test day.


Your device also needs to meet these minimums:


- **Windows:** Windows 11 version 24H2 or later, 1 GB of free storage. S mode and Windows 11 SE aren't supported.
- **Mac:** macOS 15 or later, 1 GB of free storage.
- **iPad:** iPadOS 18 or later, 250 MB of free storage.
- **Chromebook:** school-managed only, ChromeOS 144 or later, 1 GB of free storage.
- **Battery:** fully charged and able to last at least 3 hours. Bring your charger too, since outlets aren't guaranteed.
- **Screen:** at least 10 inches for laptops and 8 inches for tablets.


College Board updates these minimums each school year, so check the[device requirements page](https://bluebook.collegeboard.org/students/prepare-your-device/approved-devices) before you test. If you don't have a device, you can request to borrow one from College Board at least 30 days before test day.


### 2. Where to download Bluebook


Download Bluebook from[College Board's Bluebook site](https://bluebook.collegeboard.org/students/download-bluebook) . iPad users can also get it from the App Store. If you're testing on a school-issued device, ask your school's tech team to install it for you.


### 3. When to download Bluebook and do exam setup


Download Bluebook at least 30 days before test day. That gives you time to take a practice test, switch devices if yours doesn't work, and get help if something goes wrong.


Then complete exam setup 1 to 5 days before your test. Exam setup downloads your test to your device and creates your admission ticket. Print your admission ticket or email it to yourself, since you'll need it to get into the test center.


On the morning of the test, open Bluebook once more to check for updates or test center changes, and make sure your device is fully charged. If anything goes wrong, the[Bluebook help center](https://bluebook.collegeboard.org/students/help) walks through common fixes.


### 4. Bluebook testing tools to try before test day


Bluebook has built-in tools you'll use on test day. Try each one in a practice test first so you're not figuring them out under time pressure:


- **Desmos graphing calculator:** available for the whole Math section. You can move it and resize it.
- **Reference sheet:** common math formulas.
- **Testing timer:** shows the time left in each module. You can hide it until the last 5 minutes.
- **Highlights & Notes:** mark up passages or leave yourself notes.
- **Mark for Review:** flag a question to come back to.
- **Option Eliminator:** cross out answer choices you've ruled out.
- **Line Reader:** keeps your eyes on one line of text at a time.
- **Question menu:** jump to any question and see which ones you skipped or flagged.


Desmos is worth practicing most, since it can save real time on Math. Acely's[Desmos cheat sheet](https://acely.com/sat/desmos-cheat-sheet) and[Desmos guide library](https://acely.com/desmos-guide-library/) cover the shortcuts that come up most on the SAT.


## How to use Bluebook for SAT practice


Whether you are preparing for the AP exams[or the SAT](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wChds5oAtN4&list=PL9t_4Cr9ZvsGYZzxbmk3e48EBDVcGL1h4&index=13&pp=iAQB) , you need hours of practice with consistent full-length practice tests as a part of your study routine. Thankfully, the Bluebook testing app also comes packed with practice resources, including SAT practice tests, performance analytics, and more. Here's how to make the most of these options:


### Take full-length practice tests in Bluebook


Bluebook has 8 free full-length SAT practice tests that use the same adaptive format and tools as the real test. Sign in with your College Board account so your scores save to My Practice, where you can review every question and use Tailored Practice to get extra questions on your weaker skills.


Wondering whether Bluebook practice tests are easier or harder than the real SAT? We break it down in[Bluebook SAT practice tests vs the actual exam](https://acely.com/blog/bluebook-sat-practice-tests-vs-actual-exam-easier-or-harder) .


### Add more practice tests to your study routine


College Board offers 8 official full-length practice tests in Bluebook, so many students save one or two for the final weeks before test day and use other full-length tests before that.


Acely has[30 full-length digital SAT practice tests](https://acely.com/sat-prep) that match the Bluebook format, plus 9,000 expert-created SAT questions. After each test, Acely's study plan updates to focus on the skills you missed, and the AI tutor explains any question step by step. You can take a full-length SAT on Acely for free, no credit card required.


### Explore BigFuture


It can be hard to think beyond the upcoming exams right now, which is why taking the time to check out the "BigFuture" section will be very helpful. This gives you access to information about scholarships, careers, colleges, and more.


Of course, it doesn't directly come up as a practice test feature. Still, it is a great way to motivate yourself for the big and bright future that awaits you after the test day, and your digital SAT will be left behind.


## Get ready for test day


Bluebook takes a little getting used to, so don't leave it for the night before. Download it early, take at least one full-length practice test in the app, and complete exam setup 1 to 5 days before your test. On test day, bring your fully charged device, your charger, and your admission ticket.
